# OpenAPI Modifier

> Configure a pipeline of rules to modify an OpenAPI 3.0 or 3.1 document.
> All paths below are relative to the installed openapi-modifier package.

## Before writing a configuration

1. Inspect the existing configuration and the input OpenAPI document. Identify
   the exact operation (HTTP method and path), parameter location, and any $ref.
2. Read the relevant rule guide below and the shared guides it references.
3. Use `pipeline` entries with `rule` and `config`; preserve existing steps and
   their order. Do not use the legacy `rules`/`name` or `patch-schemas` examples
   that still appear in parts of README.md.
4. Check `dist-types/src/rules/generated-types.d.ts` for available rule names
   and the referenced declaration files for configuration fields. Use the
   installed implementation in `dist/src/rules/` to resolve documentation gaps.
   Do not invent configuration fields or assume that patch rules create targets.
5. Apply the configuration to a separate output file and inspect the actual diff.
   Check warnings: a completed command does not prove the intended target changed.

## Configuration

- [Overview and CLI usage](README.md)
- [Configuration types](dist-types/src/config.d.ts)
- [Available rules and their types](dist-types/src/rules/generated-types.d.ts)
- [Target descriptors](docs/descriptor.md)
- [Schema changes](docs/schema-diff.md)
- [Shallow merge versus deep merge](docs/merge-vs-deepmerge.md)

Minimal CommonJS configuration:

```js
module.exports = {
  pipeline: [
    // { rule: 'rule-name', config: { ... } }
  ],
};
```

Run the installed CLI from the consuming project:

```sh
./node_modules/.bin/openapi-modifier --input=input.yaml --output=output.yaml --config=openapi-modifier.config.js
```

- [Modify an existing parameter](src/rules/patch-endpoint-parameter-schema/README.md)
- [Modify a request body schema](src/rules/patch-endpoint-request-body-schema/README.md)
- [Modify a response schema](src/rules/patch-endpoint-response-schema/README.md)
- [Modify a component schema](src/rules/patch-component-schema/README.md)
- [Modify an operation](src/rules/patch-endpoint-schema/README.md)
- [Merge another specification](src/rules/merge-openapi-spec/README.md)
- [Remove a parameter](src/rules/remove-parameter/README.md)
- [Filter endpoints](src/rules/filter-endpoints/README.md)
- [Remove deprecated elements](src/rules/remove-deprecated/README.md)
- [Remove unused components](src/rules/remove-unused-components/README.md)
- [Change content types](src/rules/change-content-type/README.md)
- [Filter by content type](src/rules/filter-by-content-type/README.md)
- [Change endpoint base paths](src/rules/change-endpoints-basepath/README.md)
- [Remove operation IDs](src/rules/remove-operation-id/README.md)
- [Remove minimum item constraints](src/rules/remove-min-items/README.md)
- [Remove maximum item constraints](src/rules/remove-max-items/README.md)

## Important distinctions

- Adding a query/header/path/cookie parameter differs from adding a property
  to a request body schema. Inspect the document before choosing a rule.
- `patch-endpoint-parameter-schema` patches an existing parameter; it does not
  add a missing parameter. For additions, inspect the operation patch or merge
  rule and its array behavior before constructing the configuration.
- `merge` is shallow. `deepmerge` recursively merges and uses the underlying
  library's default array behavior. Inspect existing arrays to avoid replacing
  unrelated parameters or introducing duplicates.
- Changing a shared component may affect multiple operations. Inspect its
  references and confirm that this scope matches the user's request.
- Some rule guides link to source tests or external resources that are not
  shipped in the npm package. Use the packaged types and implementation when
  those sources are unavailable; report any remaining uncertainty explicitly.
